column2: Hand-maintained overrides, applied on top of the postal files by
scripts/pack_en.py. Use this for names the published files omit, so
re-downloading the official data never discards them.
Format: Chinese name <TAB> English. Write the Chinese as it appears in an
address; pack_en.py normalizes it the same way it does every other key.
Romanization follows Hanyu Pinyin and the conventions the postal files
- ü is written u          綠 -> Lu, 女 -> Nu (per 女中路 'Nuzhong Rd.')
- the name is joined      大埔美園區一路 -> 'Dapumeiyuanqu 1st Rd.'
- numbers become ordinals 一 -> 1st, 廿七 -> 27th
- 橫巷 -> Side Ln., 新村 -> New Vil., 山莊 -> Villa, 大樓 -> Bldg.
- a direction that modifies a complete name is abbreviated
東彰南路/東彰北路 are absent from the road file entirely (not even by
section), but the post office's own online lookup returns these.
Wrong ordinals ('3th Farm'), and one 第 transliterated as 'Di' where the
rest of its own series (下橫街第一巷..第三巷) drops it.
--- 地下層 rows the ZIP directory files under a road name --------------
data/2606_01.csv puts a floor descriptor in its ROAD column on two rows
(both streets also have a normal row of their own). Not in the official
bilingual file, so the English below is inferred from the one precedent
it does carry: 大同路地下商場 -> 'Underground Shopping Mall, Datong Rd.'
Keyed on the whole string, lane included, so the parts stay in postal
order rather than trailing the street name.
